-**SHP-4 — Submission.** The shaper ends by calling `submit` with exactly one result: `questions`, `files`, or `blocked`. A blocked result has the exact shape `{"blocked":{"paths":["relative/protected/path"],"reason":"why the requested change requires this edit"}}`; paths and reason must be nonempty, and every path must be protected by the current baseline contract, including configured globs. It is a report, never authorization. A valid blocked result writes no new Intent or approval and starts no Build; it ends with exit 1, `shape/protected_conflict: required edits touch protected files: <paths>` in submitted order, the supplied reason, and `Next: revise the request, or review and commit .kogen/project.yaml outside Build, then shape again; preserve checks and actual check configuration. There is no protected-edit override.` A manual configuration review is outside Build and changes the approval baseline; it is not approval of a protected edit. If a previous not-ready submission exists, its files retain the existing SHP-4 behavior. Validate the entire file envelope, content types, normal owned paths and uniqueness before merging; an unsafe, malformed or duplicate-path mixed payload contributes no entries. Within one conversation, well-formed proposals accumulate: latest content for a path wins, omitted paths retain earlier proposed bytes, and explicit original content reverts an edit. The files array is nonempty. Native Shape also offers `propose_files`, which retains well-formed files under the same path rules (latest content wins) in private custody under `.kogen/local/shaping/<slug>/proposed/` without checking them; it is not a submission and never counts as an invalid one, and a malformed or unsafe call retains nothing. A provider failure that stops Shape names the retained proposals. Lint, parse and readiness edits may submit only changed files; unchanged-red acknowledgments follow SHP-8. The complete accumulated package is validated before writing. An invalid submission goes back with its problems and writes nothing; well-formed proposals rejected by Intent validation remain available for correction. Previously declared proposed JavaScript steps must remain listed in `Acceptance:` and a proposed model must remain declared; abandoning these paths rejects the candidate before writing so retained executable steps cannot leave the approval baseline. Check those declarations again after formatting, before readiness or acknowledgment can certify the final package. Existing auxiliary-file ownership rules are unchanged. Omission cannot delete a proposal: preserve and park the partial package and its exclusively owned new step files, remove the now-empty Intent directory, then use normal shaping again with the same slug or a new one to discard an earlier new artifact. No deletion DSL, persistent proposal state or cross-invocation replay is provided. A valid complete merged submission is written, then the project's fixers (`commands.fix`, in order, progress `kogen: running fix-<n>: <command>`) run once in the repository root, so the Intent's files are formatted as the project formats files. The fixers' changes to the accumulated submission's files are kept: the card, the approval hash and the Build's checks on the unchanged tree see the formatted files, and the Build's own fixer rounds find nothing left to change in them. What the fixers change anywhere else is undone. The files are then checked for readiness (SHP-8); if the checks find problems, those go back to the shaper in the same way, and its next attempt overwrites the complete accumulated files, preserving omitted proposals. After a not-ready attempt the shaper may also ask questions (SHP-6); the files of that attempt stay. Invalid and not-ready submissions share one counter: at the third failed submission in a row shaping stops (exit 1). After an invalid one it prints `shape/invalid_output: the shaper's output was not a valid Intent after 3 attempts` plus the last problems. After a not-ready one it prints `intent/not_ready` (SHP-8), and the files of that last attempt stay. A tool-free answer is not a submission and is not charged to that counter: it is counted separately as a no-tool turn, and the next inference alone requires the terminal `submit` tool in the API request (Responses `tool_choice` `{"type":"function","name":"submit"}`, Chat Completions `{"type":"function","function":{"name":"submit"}}`) while the reminder `End by calling submit with either questions or files.` is still sent. A route that cannot force a tool (Anthropic adaptive thinking) and an external executor keep the reminder or feedback only, with no thinking, model or effort change and no forced wire request. The third no-tool answer stops shaping (exit 1) with `shape/invalid_output: the shaper answered without calling any tool 3 times (no-tool limit); no submission was made`, not a claim of refused submissions. Both counters accumulate over local working-window resets, which also carry any pending enforcement. Every enforced request is recorded as a `forced_submit_turn` event (owner, target tool, provider, whether the API forces it, both counters), and each native invocation exit records `shaping_turn_counts` (owner, `no_tool_turns`, `invalid_submissions`, the final refusal included). Files may only be the Intent's own files and step files named `<steps_dir>/<slug>__<suffix>.js` (nonempty suffix), new or existing: shaping may prepare edits to an existing step file of that name, which the caller reviews with the Intent before approval and which is then fixed for the Build (VER-1). Any other path under `steps_dir`, such as a generic `features/steps/is_even_steps.js`, is an invalid submission with the problem `<path>: new step files must be named <steps_dir>/<slug>__<suffix>.js (nonempty suffix); prefix step sentences and definitions with <slug>: `. Before readiness, the step self-check reports `step sentence must start with <slug>: `, `definition must start with <slug>: ` or `binding comes from a step file outside this Intent: <file>` for a step that breaks this namespace, and nothing is published. Every shaping progress line includes elapsed whole seconds since shaping started; a model request is printed as `kogen: shaping (request 2, 95 s)`.
